# requireNonObject

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not an object.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonObject() — Returns the value after checking that it is not an object. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonObject<T>(
  value: T | object,
  message: string = "Expected a non-object value."
): T;
```

The test is `typeof value === "object"` with `null` excluded, so arrays, dates and class instances all count, while a function does not. `isObjectLike` is the one that also accepts functions.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                 | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                   | `T \| object` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-object value."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with an object excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition               |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is an object. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonObject(null); // => null
requireNonObject("abc"); // => "abc"
requireNonObject({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonObject([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
